p:ARM: Armenia uses the dram, issued by the Central Bank of Armenia, which scores 21 of 100 on exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed. The dram is held on a pre-announced crawling peg against the US dollar, meaning the rate is moved in small announced steps. One case is recorded and it is unproven. In February 2022 Armbusinessbank's new ownership was registered as MFM Global Invest LLC of Switzerland with 74.998 per cent and Housing for Young Families, a refinancing credit organisation founded by the Central Bank of Armenia itself, with 25.001 per cent. Former labour minister Maneh Tandilyan called the deal non-transparent and a gross violation of the law that bars the regulator from interfering in the activities of commercial banks; the bank gave no comment to the news agency that reported it, and no inquiry or ruling has followed, so it stands as a claim rather than a finding. One career move runs both ways: Tigran Davtyan held managerial roles at the bank from 1994 to 1998 and later ran two commercial banks, as chief executive of Converse Bank from 2009 to 2016 and of Inecobank from 2018 to 2019, and has been an independent non-executive director of Ameriabank since July 2020. No government pressure was reported in the 37 quarters surveyed between 2010 and 2018. The bank has rejoined the World Bank Treasury's Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership, having been a member from 2006 to 2014; what it gets is advice, onsite expertise and staff training rather than management of its assets. It has one swap line with China, an arrangement for two central banks to lend each other currency, for 77 billion drams and one billion yuan, dated March 2015, though whether it is still in force is not known. A bank representative says Giesecke+Devrient won the printing of its third banknote series after an evaluation of all offers. KPMG Armenia LLC audits the accounts.
p:HTI: The Bank of the Republic of Haiti, created in 1979, issues the currency HTG, held at a de facto peg to the US dollar as of December 2025; the dollar is also listed as a currency there. Its exposure score is 35 of 100, where 0 means shielded from outside influence and 100 means fully exposed; that is more exposed than 66% of 194 places. Corruption and secrecy around it scores 82, with a Corruption Perceptions Index score of 16 of 100 and money-laundering risk of 8.12 of 10 (rank 2 of 177, where 1 is riskiest). Written independence from government scores 0.366 of 1 on one index (rank 151 of 155) and 0.376 on another (rank 165 of 191). Government pressure was reported in 0 of 37 quarters from 2010 to 2018. One case is recorded: in April 2004 justice minister Bernard Gousse barred Venel Joseph, a former governor of the bank, from leaving the country, naming him among 37 former officials to be kept available for investigations into crimes alleged against the government of ousted president Jean-Bertrand Aristide, and calling the travel ban an insurance policy. What conduct at the bank, if any, was being looked into is not reported, and no charge and no finding followed. The bank's accounts are audited by KPMG S.A. of France together with the Port-au-Prince firm Merove-Pierre - Cabinet d'Experts-Comptables, whose joint report on the year ended 30 September 2021 was signed on 30 June 2022.
p:SYC: The Central Bank of Seychelles, set up in 1983, issues the Seychelles rupee and, as of December 2025, holds it within a band of plus or minus 2 percent against the US dollar. It scores 27 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence, below three-quarters of the places measured; its weakest side is corruption and secrecy around it, at 49, from laws that hide who owns money and money-laundering risk in its banks. One case is recorded and it rests on an anonymous accusation. Pierre Laporte left the governorship in March 2012 to become finance minister, and in September 2012 an anonymous letter accused him of drawing two salaries at once, one from the central bank and one from the government. He denied wrongdoing and said he had negotiated a severance package to offset the lower ministerial pay. No charge, inquiry or ruling is reported. Part of its foreign currency savings is handled by outsiders. The World Bank's Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership runs a portfolio of its reserves, first funded with 100 million US dollars in 2019 and still held at the end of 2025, and during 2025 it also ran workshops and executive forums and paid for staff qualifications. Crown Agents Investment Management runs a bond portfolio split evenly between US dollars and Chinese renminbi, begun in 2014 with 25.0 million US dollars and topped up by another 25.0 million in April 2022. UBS Asset Management runs a money market fund holding part of the reserves, first funded with 10.0 million US dollars in 2017 and still held at the end of 2025, and has invited bank staff to its annual reserves seminar. A trade report says the bank's new family of banknotes was printed by the British printers De La Rue, giving no contract value, volume or term. The 2025 accounts were audited by the Auditor General of Seychelles, with the audit review carried out by Grant Thornton Audit and Accounting Limited in Abu Dhabi.
p:VNM: The State Bank of Vietnam issues the dong and moves its rate against the dollar in small steps rather than leaving it to the market. On paper its law gives it almost no independence, 0.301 of 1 and 154th of 155 places, and government pressure was reported in 6 of 37 quarters up to 2018. That weakness is written into the statute itself and is still in force. Under the Law on the State Bank of Vietnam of 16 June 2010, in force from 1 January 2011, the bank is a ministerial-level agency of the Government as well as the central bank; the National Assembly decides the annual inflation target, on the Government's proposal, and the Prime Minister or the Governor then decides which tools to use, following rules the Government sets. There is no episode and no end date here: the bank carries out a target set above it. In April 2024 the Ho Chi Minh City People's Court sentenced Truong My Lan, chair of Van Thinh Phat, to death for fraud at Saigon Commercial Bank, finding that she had ordered subordinates to bribe State Bank inspectors; state media reported that head banking inspector Do Thi Nhan took 5.2 million US dollars and deputy chief inspector Nguyen Van Hung 300,000. In October 2011 Securency, a subsidiary of the Reserve Bank of Australia, pleaded guilty in the Supreme Court of Victoria to conspiring to give benefits to foreign public officials to win banknote business with Vietnam's note-issuing authority between 2001 and 2004; the officials are not named. The bank's notes are printed by the state-owned National Banknote Printing Factory, whose chairman the Governor appoints. Cao Si Kiem, governor from 1989 to 1997, joined the board of the joint-stock commercial DongA Bank in March 2012 and became its chairman on 26 April 2014. The bank is one of the 63 central banks that own the Bank for International Settlements, and Vietnam scores 35 of 100 on exposure to outside influence.
p:BGR: Bulgaria's central bank is the Bulgarian National Bank. On 1 January 2026 the country swapped the lev for the euro at 1.95583 lev to the euro and joined the Eurosystem, the group of national central banks that works with the European Central Bank, so its governor now sits on the body that sets interest rates. Its own large case concerns Corporate Commercial Bank, Corpbank, which collapsed in June 2014: prosecutors charged two former deputy governors responsible for supervision with failing, from February 2010, to take the measures the law required against the bank, allegedly to benefit its shareholders. Gounev was charged in June 2014 and removed from office by court order that December, and Simeonov about ten months later; neither charge is proven, and the accusation that Corpbank's majority owner embezzled 206 million leva is likewise unproven. The state's Bulgarian National Audit Office checks the books under a continuing legal mandate, Oberthur Fiduciaire AD has handled banknote production since 2014, and Louisenthal supplied the thread, foil and watermark for the 100-lev note that became legal tender on 28 December 2018. The bank is one of the 63 central banks that own the Bank for International Settlements, and belongs to the World Bank Treasury's Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership, which offers advice, training or asset management without the page saying which Bulgaria uses. About 60 per cent of its 41 tonnes of gold sits outside its own vaults, stored at the Bank of England, which stores the metal rather than managing it. Two findings sit at the European Central Bank: the European Ombudsman found maladministration over President Mario Draghi's membership of the Group of Thirty, a forum whose members include private bankers, and recommended in January 2018 that he suspend it, which the ECB declined; and a speech by Coeure to a private London event on 18 May 2015 about front-loading asset purchases was published only the following morning, which the ECB called an internal procedure error. Kalin Hristov, long a member of the Governing Council and deputy governor for the Issue Department, joined the supervisory board of the commercial DSK Bank in August 2025; no ethics finding is recorded. Bulgaria scores 32 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence. On 5 March 2015 Parliament voted 84 to 0 to set up an ad hoc committee of inquiry into the collapse of Corporate Commercial Bank, to examine the conduct of the state bodies and institutions meant by law to exercise the control that should have prevented the bank being drained, over the years 2009 to 2014. The Bulgarian National Bank's banking supervision arm is named among those bodies. Before that, on 10 December 2014, the bank published a letter from the European Central Bank signed by Mario Draghi warning that proposed amendments to the deposit insurance law could infringe its independence. The amendments would have obliged the bank to cover any shortfall in the deposit guarantee fund. The letter said the draft would stop the bank investing and managing its own reserves, that transfers to the fund could cut its own resources enough to hinder the work it does within the European System of Central Banks, and that such a transfer could put the stability of Bulgaria's currency board at risk.
p:GUY: The Bank of Guyana issues the Guyanese dollar, held at what is in practice a fixed rate to the US dollar as of December 2025. It scores 30 of 100 on exposure to outside influence, where 0 means shielded and 100 fully exposed, and the weakest side is corruption and secrecy around it, at 56, with the country scoring 40 of 100 on the Corruption Perceptions Index. Independence written into its law scores 0.609 of 1, ranking 93 of 191, and no government pressure was reported in 37 quarters from 2010 to 2018. No case at the bank is recorded, which is not proof none happened. One career move is on record, and it is entirely within the public sector, so it is listed but not counted: governor Gobind Ganga directed the bank's research department from 1995 to November 2003, left to be an alternate executive director at the World Bank in Washington, returned as deputy governor in June 2005 and became governor on 2 December 2014. No private employer appears anywhere in the career the bank publishes. Crane Currency is listed as having supplied banknotes, banknote paper and anti-counterfeiting features, though that comes from a client list in another body's announcement rather than a contract notice. The Auditor General audits the accounts.
p:MKD: North Macedonia's money is the denar, issued by the National Bank of the Republic of North Macedonia and held in practice at a fixed rate to the euro. It scores 24 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence, and its weakest side is corruption and secrecy around it. Its notes are printed abroad, by three firms in turn. The bank contracted the French firm Oberthur Fiduciaire to print 100-denar notes, reported on 8 May 2026, for 59,800,000 denars, about 972,358 euros. It had contracted the Russian state company Goznak for the 100-denar notes in 2021, for about 400,000 euros, as part of a 2.2 million euro reissue carrying the state's changed constitutional name. Three separate contracts with De La Rue International cover the 10, 500 and 1,000 denar notes, 45 million notes for 3.775 million euros in total, 20 million of them polymer. One case is recorded, running from 2017 to 2020, and it is unproven: an association of depositors of Eurostandard Bank said in a press release that the governor tipped off the finance minister and other large depositors so they could take their money out before the bank was put under administration, and that financial police reports were kept secret so it could keep operating. The association said Finance Minister Nina Angelovska withdrew more than 200,000 euros months before the central bank acted, and that over 60 million euros were lost; no charges and no official finding are reported. The European Central Bank gave the bank a temporary line to borrow euros against collateral from 15 December 2022 to 15 January 2024, which has expired. One career move is on record and it too stays outside the private sector, so it is listed but not counted: governor Anita Angelovska Bezhoska spent about eight years at the Ministry of Finance, ending as manager of the treasury department, and was state secretary in 2003 and 2004, then worked as an economist at the International Monetary Fund in Washington before joining the bank as chief economist, serving almost eight years as vice-governor and becoming governor in May 2018. The page the bank publishes names no private firm and no commercial bank.
p:PNG: The Bank of Papua New Guinea issues the kina, whose rate against the US dollar is shifted in small steps rather than left to the market, and the country scores 41 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence. One case is on record. Court documents obtained by the journalism group OCCRP show that the National Fraud and Anti-Corruption Directorate searched the bank's offices in August and September 2023 in a money-laundering investigation into Genia, then acting governor; she won a temporary halt that was later dismissed, she has not been charged, and it remains under investigation and unproven. She had earlier been under fraud-squad investigation over a firearms deal for the bank's security team, and became governor in early 2024. The government had already put the bank's own law under review. On 13 May 2021 Treasurer Ian Ling-Stuckey, with the Prime Minister and the Ministerial Economic Committee of the National Executive Council, issued terms of reference for a review of the Central Banking Act 2000 that was told to examine whether the Governor should keep his sole power to decide monetary policy under section 10, and to reconsider the bank's governance and the length of senior management terms. In April 2024 the Prime Minister announced new board members, among them Sir Robin Fleming, former chief executive of the commercial bank Bank South Pacific, and Mark Baker, former country head of the commercial bank Australia and New Zealand Banking. The 2024 annual report names Pictet Asset Management as the weakest of the outside firms running part of the reserves that year, with DWS and BlackRock the strongest. Note Printing Australia listed the bank among its export orders in 2006 and 2007.
p:TWN: The Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) issues the New Taiwan dollar, and its notes are made by the Central Engraving and Printing Plant; a bank press release on the NT$200 note says that note was printed by China Engraving & Printing Works. Independence written into its law is low: 0.454 of 1 on one index and 0.194 on another, with the rules on lending to the government scored 0 and 0.03. No government pressure was reported from 2010 to 2018, and no documented case at the bank was found. Where the bank sits is itself on record: under the revised Central Bank of China Act promulgated on 8 November 1979 it is a state bank and an agency under the Executive Yuan, the cabinet, rather than a body standing outside the executive branch, and its own official history records that it has been there since that reorganisation. The Act leaves rate and policy decisions with the bank's board, so what this describes is the institution's place in the machinery of government rather than a transfer of the policy power, and it has no end date. One overlap is recorded rather than a move: 陳思寬 (Chen Szu-kuan) sits on the bank's 21st Board of Directors for a term running from 27 January 2025 to 26 January 2030 while, by the bank's own list of directors, serving as chairman of SinoPac Financial Holdings Company Limited and of SinoPac Securities Investment Trust Company Limited; that list says nothing about who owns them. The bank holds 423.9 tonnes of gold. Taiwan scores 24 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence, its weak point being corruption and secrecy around it.
p:CUB: The Central Bank of Cuba issues the currency CUP. Its exposure score is 35 of 100, where 0 means shielded from outside influence and 100 means fully exposed; that is more exposed than 68% of 194 places. Corruption and secrecy around it scores 57, with a Corruption Perceptions Index score of 40 of 100. Written independence from government is low: 0.354 of 1 on one index (rank 153 of 155) and 0.262 on another (rank 180 of 191). On public transparency it scores 1.5 of 15 (rank 109 of 112). Government pressure was reported in 0 of 37 quarters from 2010 to 2018, but the arrangement that matters here is in the law. Decree-Law 361 of 2018, issued by the Council of State and published in the Gaceta Oficial on 12 October 2018 in place of Decree-Law 172 of 1997, requires the bank to design monetary policy in step with the government's fiscal and macroeconomic aims, under an annual policy agreement signed by ministers. It has no end date. One case is documented, and it is still under investigation: in late September 2026 an investigation in Santiago de Cuba concerned workers at two state banks, Banco Popular de Ahorro and BANDEC, both supervised by the Banco Central de Cuba, with reports saying the workers handed out cash in exchange for electronic transfers, charging commissions of between 30 and 50 per cent, acting together with self-employed people. Cash, banknote counting machines, magnetic cards and documents were reported seized, and no amounts, names or number of detainees were made public. The central bank's Minister-President, Juana Lilia Delgado Portal, issued an official note rejecting the conduct, ordering that any complaint be investigated without delay, and calling for administrative, labour and criminal responsibility to be established, internal controls strengthened and whistleblowers protected. No charges or outcomes had been announced.
p:SDN: The Central Bank of Sudan issues the Sudanese pound. It scores 43 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed, and its weakest side is corruption and secrecy around it, at 85. In October 2025 Sovereignty Council head Abdel Fattah al-Burhan dismissed governor Burai Al-Siddiq Ali Ahmed after a dispute over the rules for buying and exporting gold, and appointed Amna Mirghani Hassan El Toum; deputy governor Mohamed Osman Ahmed Mohamed Khair was dismissed less than two weeks later. Government pressure was reported in 2 of 37 quarters from 2010 to 2018, both times pressing the bank to cut rates or ease and demanding that it print money. Its law scores 0.333 of 1 on one measure of independence, ranking 172 of 191, and it scores 1.5 of 15 on how much it tells the public. Its notes are made in the country: Dabanga reported in February 2019 that Sudan's new 200-pound banknote had gone into production at the Sudanese Company for Currency Printing, a domestic press the prime minister had visited that week. Who checks its books is now on record, and it is the state rather than a firm: the bank's annual report presents its balance sheet, profit and loss account, statement of changes in owner equity and cash flow statement for the year ended 31 December 2015 as audited by the National Audit Chamber. That is the body behind the Central Bank of Sudan Act 2002, which requires the accounts to be audited in accordance with the General Audit Chambers Act 1999 without naming an auditor. No documented case at the central bank was found.
p:ARE: The Central Bank of the United Arab Emirates issues the dirham and holds it at a fixed rate against the US dollar, an arrangement called a peg. It scores 30 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed. On Saturday 29 August 2026 the bank said it had ordered a special and urgent examination of the UAE branches of Banque Misr, an Egyptian lender with five branches in the country, after the United States raised money-laundering concerns; the US Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network had proposed a rule that would revoke Banque Misr UAE's correspondent banking access to US financial institutions. The bank said the examination includes a forensic, in-depth lookback over the period covered by the US statement and focuses on transactions of the companies named in it, that it was studying options for the bank's status if the US special measure is formally imposed, and that it expects banks it licenses to avoid reputational risks to the financial system and to respect other countries' laws. Nothing has been proven against Banque Misr; these are concerns raised by the US authorities and an examination ordered by the UAE central bank. The same report noted that in June 2026 a foreign bank branch in the UAE, not named, was fined 20 million dirhams, about 5.44 million US dollars, for anti-money-laundering failures. No government pressure was reported in the 37 quarters surveyed between 2010 and 2018. Its law gives it middling independence, 0.685 of 1, and the cabinet's hold on it is written into that law. Under Decretal Federal Law No. 14 of 2018, board members are appointed by federal decree on the Cabinet's recommendation and their membership can be ended by federal decree with the Cabinet's approval, the exchange rate regime is set only on a board proposal with Cabinet approval, and the bank cannot withdraw a currency denomination from circulation without Cabinet approval. There is no episode and no end date: this is how the bank is arranged. It is one of the 63 central banks that own the Bank for International Settlements. Its notes are printed by Oumolat Security Printing, which the Emirates Investment Authority started and owned before it was transferred to the central bank; a new 100 dirham polymer note printed by Oumolat was reported on 31 March 2025. Abdulhamid Saeed, made governor by federal decree on 2 April 2020, had been group chief executive of First Abu Dhabi Bank.
p:LAO: The Bank of the Lao P.D.R. is the central bank of Laos, which uses the kip; its top-denomination 100,000-kip note is printed by Goznak, the Russian state currency works. One case is recorded and it ended in convictions. On 8 September 2026 the Vientiane People's Court sentenced two former directors general to life imprisonment for abusing their positions to withdraw foreign currency from the bank's reserves and exchange unlimited amounts; one of them, Aod, was sentenced in his absence because he died during the proceedings. In a related case nine bank employees were convicted of corruption and money laundering, including trading currency at special rates. Losses across the cases exceeded 2.29 trillion kip, about 102.6 million US dollars. Government pressure was reported in 1 of 37 quarters between 2010 and 2018, and that instance was a demand to print money. The government's hold on the bank is in its founding law and has no end date. Under the Law on the National Bank of the Lao P.D.R., approved on 14 October 1995, a Deputy Prime Minister chairs the bank's Board of Management, with the Governor and the Minister of Finance as vice-chairs; the Prime Minister appoints and removes board members; and the Governor proposes monetary, interest rate and exchange rate policy to that board and then submits it to the Government, which decides whether to adopt and proclaim it. The bank has two swap lines with China, arrangements to borrow each other's currency: one of 6 billion yuan, and one from January 2020 with no amount stated. Laos scores 39 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:SWE: Sveriges Riksbank is Sweden's central bank and issues the krona. It scores 15 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence, less exposed than 99 per cent of the 194 places with a figure. The Riksdag adopted a new Sveriges Riksbank Act on 23 November 2022, in force from 1 January 2023. The inquiry that preceded it proposed limits on what the Riksbank may do in monetary policy, which its Executive Board objected to in its consultation response and some of which were dropped from the final Act. What stayed includes a requirement of exceptional grounds before the bank may buy or sell financial instruments other than Swedish government securities for monetary policy purposes, on the reasoning that such trading carries much greater financial risk for the bank and for state finances; limits on its equity and a cap on borrowing for the foreign exchange reserve; and an obligation to ask the Riksdag to restore its equity when that falls below the floor, which it had to do after the bond purchases it made earlier lost money as rates rose. The Riksdag also now approves the specification of the inflation target. The bank's own account is two-sided: it says the Act leaves it a strong and clear mandate and carries the ban on taking instructions over unchanged, while governor Erik Thedeen said after a year of it that the governance is too strong on strengthening the foreign exchange reserve and on buying securities for financial stability purposes. Two linked cases run from 2020 to 2021. On 18 June 2021 the Riksbank said a routine check of staff securities dealings had found a few employees making transactions that did not fit its ethics rules, including share trades close to monetary policy decisions and trades in companies whose corporate bonds it was buying; it called this inappropriate, held talks with those involved and began revising the rules. After media reports that Stefan Ingves and Skingsley had conflicts of interest from shares they held while deciding on corporate bond purchases, the bank's General Council reviewed the matter and on 17 December 2021 concluded the link was too weak to amount to a conflict of interest, finding no shortcoming in their conduct. Ingves was appointed governor in October 2005, having headed a department at the International Monetary Fund since 1999; that move is not an accusation. The Riksbank's own published CV shows a move the other way: Anna Breman was a senior economist at Swedbank from 2013 to 2015 and its group chief economist from 2015 to 2019, then became deputy governor of the Riksbank in 2019 and first deputy governor in 2022. Swedbank is a commercial bank listed on the Stockholm exchange rather than a state body. Its 125.7 tonnes of gold sit partly at the Riksbank and partly abroad, 61.4 tonnes at the Bank of England, 33.2 at the Bank of Canada, 13.2 at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York and 2.8 at the Swiss National Bank, which is storage of the gold and not management of its money. Crane AB printed the notes at Tumba until the Riksbank gave notice to end the contract on 19 June 2018 because Crane was moving printing to Malta; De La Rue replaced it under an agreement announced on 19 September 2018.
p:KEN: The Central Bank of Kenya is the country's central bank and issues its money. Three cases are on file. In the Goldenberg scandal, the government paid cash subsidies for fictitious gold and diamond exports under President Daniel arap Moi. In March 2006 prosecutors indicted five people, including former governor Kotut and former deputy governor Riungu. They are charged, which is unproven. On 23 March 2006 governor Andrew Mullei was charged with four counts of abuse of office, including hiring his son as a consultant. He denied awarding Sh9 million in contracts irregularly, and no court outcome was found. From 2015 to 2018, Kenya's anti-corruption commission investigated current and former officials over the collapse of Imperial Bank, whose directors said bank officers helped embezzle Sh34 billion. That is under investigation and unproven. One career move is on record. A Kenyan government sector profile says Sheila M'mbijjewe was appointed deputy governor by the President in June 2015 and sat on the bank's Monetary Policy Committee for nine years, and that she had served on the boards of several companies, as a director of Standard Chartered Bank, a non-executive director of Ecobank and a board member of PricewaterhouseCoopers; it gives no dates for those roles. Kenya scores 38 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:PAK: The State Bank of Pakistan is the country's central bank. It scores 29 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence. One case from 2025 is alleged and unproven. In August 2025 Pakistan Observer reported, citing internal memos and cash slips, that senior officials including an executive director issued bulk fresh banknotes directly to private brokers, who resold them at premiums, with each transaction netting officials at least 2 million rupees in kickbacks. It said no probe had been opened. In January 2014 governor Yaseen Anwar resigned; the Finance Ministry spokesman said he cited personal reasons, while unnamed senior officials said it covered differences with Finance Minister Ishaq Dar over inflation and reserves. Anwar had come to the bank from private finance, and the bank's own profile of him gives the dates: he trained at JPMorgan Chase in New York from 1973 to 1975, spent about fifteen years at Bank of America from 1976 to 1991 ending as a vice president in its global export finance group, was a vice president at Merrill Lynch in New York and London from 1992 to 2001, and was a non-executive director of United National Bank Ltd. (U.K.) from 2000 to 2006, before being appointed deputy governor on 29 March 2007 and governor on 19 October 2011. Two governors came from the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund: Ishrat Husain, appointed in December 1999, and Reza Baqir, appointed in May 2019 after leading the IMF's Debt Policy Division. KPMG and BDO audit its accounts.
p:BGD: Bangladesh Bank issues the taka, printed at Gazipur by the Security Printing Corporation (Bangladesh) Ltd, known locally as Takshal. On the night of 4 February 2016 attackers used the bank's access to SWIFT, the network banks use to send payment instructions, to take reserves from its account at the New York Federal Reserve: 101 million dollars by The Daily Star's figure, 81 million extracted by Prothom Alo's. A government inquiry's final report of 30 May 2016 hinted that central bank officials were involved, but it was never published and no one had been punished as of 2019. Governor Atiur Rahman resigned on 15 March 2016, having been criticised for not telling Finance Minister Abul Maal Abdul Muhith, who called the bank's handling very incompetent. The Anti-Corruption Commission prosecuted Atiur in February 2025 over the AnonTex loan scam and in June 2025 opened an investigation into him over alleged abuse of power and the Hallmark and S Alam Group frauds; former deputy governor SK Sur was arrested on 14 January 2025 for failing to submit an asset statement, after a 2022 investigation into allegations he helped and gained from PK Halder's loan scam. Neither is proven. Governor Abdur Rouf Talukder resigned on 9 August 2024 citing health, three days after more than a hundred of the bank's own staff stormed his office demanding he go. Its gold is stored abroad rather than managed for it: the Bank of England holds about 188,927 troy ounces, used in lending, Standard Chartered 92,739 ounces and HSBC 93,535. One career move runs out of the bank into private banking: Md. Khurshid Alam joined Bangladesh Bank as an assistant director in 1988, worked in banking regulation, bank inspection and small-business programmes, was made deputy governor in February 2024 on a three-year contract and forced to resign that August after the political transition, and was appointed chairman of Islami Bank Bangladesh PLC, which the report calls a private sector bank, on 24 May 2026. Bangladesh scores 41 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed. Bangladesh Bank's own accounts are audited by two Dhaka firms together, Howladar Yunus & Co. and ACNABIN, whose joint report for 2024-2025 was signed on 26 August 2025 and is addressed to the Government rather than to the bank's board.
p:AGO: The National Bank of Angola issues the kwanza (AOA). Angola scores 42 of 100 on exposure to influence, where 0 means shielded and 100 means fully exposed; its weakest side is secrecy about who owns money and corruption (index score 32 of 100). Government pressure was reported in 29 of 37 quarters from 2010 to 2018, nearly all pressing the bank to cut rates or ease, with 8 threats to replace leaders. On 14 August 2020 the Supreme Court convicted former governor Valter Filipe (eight years), BNA manager Samalia (five years), José Filomeno dos Santos (five years) and businessman Sebastião (six years) of embezzlement, fraud and influence peddling over an attempted transfer of $500 million to a London account, which a British bank blocked. The Constitutional Court is also named in the case. Goznak, the Russian state printer, printed the 5,000-kwanza note. KPMG audits the bank's accounts, and signed off on the 2021 accounts with one reservation and seven emphases, against three reservations and six emphases the year before. The London firm Gemcorp Capital held 56 percent of the bank's external assets at the end of 2023, 601,697 million kwanzas or about 725 million US dollars. For the 2019 and 2020 accounts Gemcorp did not say what it had invested the central bank's money in, so the bank had to carry the holding at nil, and it then renewed the investment for a further six years. Both facts come from the newspaper Expansao reading the bank's accounts rather than from the accounts themselves: the bank's own website publishes no documents a reader can open. On Friday 27 October 2017 President Joao Lourenco exonerated Valter Filipe as governor of the Banco Nacional de Angola and named Jose de Lima Massano in his place, returning Massano to the post he had held until January 2015 and taking him from the chairmanship of the executive board of Banco Angolano de Investimentos. A note from the President's Civil House says the exoneration was at Filipe's own request, and no other official reason is given; the exit came eleven days after the President criticised the bank in a speech on 16 October, and no connection between the two is reported. Massano's own career is on record: he was governor for close to ten years between 2010 and 2023, became a Senior Minister in the President's office in June 2023, and had earlier been chief executive of Banco BAI and an executive director of the state-owned BPC. His biography gives no dates for either bank. BAI's ownership is now on record from the bank's own corporate page, which says it was founded on 14 November 1996 as the first private bank with national capital established in Angola, so that side of the career is private finance. The move back is dated too: BAI's general assembly elected Massano to its board of directors on 18 August 2015, duties he had held there before, and he was due to take office on 1 September 2015. Moving between jobs is not wrongdoing.
p:URY: Uruguay's money is the peso, issued by the Central Bank of Uruguay and held within a moving band of 2 per cent or less against the US dollar as of December 2025. It scores 17 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence, and its weakest side is corruption and secrecy around it, at 43, although the country scores 73 of 100 on the Corruption Perceptions Index. One case is recorded, from 2017, and it was dismissed: prosecutor Rodrigo Morosoli, investigating the Cambio Nelson fraud at a currency exchange house, sought the formal indictment of Humberto Capote, a former president of the bank, for taking part in a continuing crime of misappropriation. Judge Marcelo Souto freed Capote at first instance, finding the evidence insufficient to prosecute him, and the prosecutor appealed in April 2017. No government pressure was reported in the 37 quarters surveyed from 2010 to 2018. The accounts are audited by the Tribunal de Cuentas under the 1995 charter law. The bank is also named among the central bank clients of a fixed-income fund built around environmental and social standards, developed jointly by Amundi and the Latin American Reserve Fund; it invests in that fund rather than handing them its reserves to manage. Three people have moved between the bank and outside jobs. Guillermo Tolosa confirmed in December 2024 that he would preside over the bank once Yamandu Orsi took office as president of Uruguay; he had worked as an economist at the International Monetary Fund and as a consultant at Oxford Economics, and was academic director of the research centre Ceres from 2018 to 2020. Washington Ribeiro spent 15 years on the bank's board, as director from June 2010 to March 2020, vice president from March 2020 to July 2024 and president from July 2024 to March 2025, and on 7 April 2026 he started as head of Uruguayan macro and sovereign strategy at the Uruguayan brokerage Latin Securities. Diego Labat, president of the bank from 2020 to 2024, was named general manager of the Bolsa Electronica de Valores by its board on 20 August 2025, replacing a man who had held the post for 25 years. The exchange was founded in January 1993 by 26 financial institutions operating in Uruguay, both public and private, so how far this is a move into private finance is not clear-cut.
n:National Audit Chamber of Sudan: The National Audit Chamber of Sudan is a state body in Khartoum. It audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Sudan, which means checking the bank's books from outside and reporting on them. The bank's own annual report presents its balance sheet, profit and loss account, statement of changes in owner equity and cash flow statement for the year ended 31 December 2015 as audited by the Chamber. This is not a contract with an end date but a duty written into law: the Central Bank of Sudan Act 2002 requires the accounts to be audited in accordance with the General Audit Chambers Act 1999, naming the statute rather than the auditor, and the bank's report names the body doing the work. One thing worth keeping in view is that the auditor here is part of the same state the bank belongs to, rather than a firm hired from outside it.
